title: Strict flat quotient systems compute simultaneous tensor and geometric inverse image
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be sites small relative to their module universes, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $R\to B_n$ compatible algebra maps to a strict ring tower $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ indexed by $n\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the category of whole semilinear module systems, with componentwise exactness, tensor and its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $\mathcal P(R)$ be the full category of unbounded cochain complexes of $R$-modules which are K-flat and have flat terms [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For $P\in\mathcal P(R)$ set $D_B(P)_n=P\otimes_RB_n$, with the quotient-induced transitions $1\otimes(B_{n+1}\to B_n)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $D_B(P)$ is a K-flat complex with flat terms in $\mathscr S(B)$, and every level is K-flat with flat terms over $B_n$. The functor $D_B$ takes quasi-isomorphisms in $\mathcal P(R)$ to componentwise quasi-isomorphisms and computes coherent derived scalar extension of the constant system $P$ to $B_\bullet$.

For $P,Q\in\mathcal P(R)$ the strict system
$$Z_T(P,Q)_n=\operatorname{Tot}\bigl((P\otimes_RB_n)\otimes_{B_n}(Q\otimes_RB_n)\bigr)$$
computes the tensor of their coherent derived reductions in $D(\mathscr S(B))$, with direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism, meaning an adjoint pair $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits, and put $C_n=u^{-1}B_n$. The strict system $Z_F(P)_n=u^{-1}(P\otimes_RB_n)$ computes the whole-system derived inverse image of that reduction in $D(\mathscr S(C))$.

These computations come with representative comparison isomorphisms natural for all cochain maps of the displayed inputs, as isomorphisms of whole derived systems [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The transition of $Z_T$ sends $a\otimes b$ to $\tau_P(a)\otimes\tau_Q(b)$, and the transition of $Z_F$ is $u^{-1}\tau_P$. The maps induced by cochain maps commute strictly with these transitions. Both $Z_T$ and $Z_F$ carry quasi-isomorphisms of the good inputs to componentwise quasi-isomorphisms. No flatness or surjectivity of the ring transitions is assumed.

proof.text: Use the unchanged constant-ring, ring-map, reduction and tensor constructions from def-pur-quotient-reduction-core. Instantiate the existing normalized scalar model on the sequence ring map and at every level. Translate its unit and cochain transpose equations to ScalarData. The ordinary slice comparison is precisely lem-pur-quotient-ordinary-models.

The constant functor sends a good input to a flat-term K-flat complex by lem-pur-quotient-constant-kflat. Apply scalar-extension K-flat preservation to its prescribed object and map functions. Flatness of each term is preserved by the ordinary scalar flatness lemma. This constructs good. Evaluate this whole-system good complex using lem-pur-system-evaluation-kflat to construct level_good. Transport along the canonical complex isomorphism induced by the evaluation-functor equality, using invariance of K-flatness and flatness under isomorphism.

The constant functor is exact, so it preserves a quasi-isomorphism. The existing scalar model preserves this map between K-flat constant complexes and its counit is invertible on each K-flat constant complex. Exact evaluation gives the componentwise quasi-isomorphism clause. These construct quasiIso and computes without a second derived pullback choice.

For tensor_quasiIso factor the map of whole-system tensors as tensor(f,id) followed by tensor(id,g). Apply the proved Generic.kflat helper giving both fixed-factor K-flat preservation clauses of lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs to the good reductions. Composition is a quasi-isomorphism, and exact evaluation preserves it.

Evaluation preserves the countable coproducts defining total tensor, because strict-system colimits are componentwise and the strict-system/sequence-site equivalence preserves colimits. In each degree define the inverse of the recorded chain comparison by the coproduct of its ordinary tensor comparison. Its two inverse identities are checked after the total-summand inclusions using TensorComparisonModel.summand and the ordinary inverse identities. Thus tensor_level holds for all complexes. The recorded tensorModelIso then supplies quotientTensorComparison.

The actual scalar-extension section equals the ordinary adjunction unit by unit_section and cancellation of the model object equality. Naturality of that sheaf map on the horizontal arrow gives reduction_transition, since the constant input has identity horizontal maps. The already proved tensor transition formula is presheaf tensor restriction followed by the sheafification unit. Exact inverse image and its normalized ordinary evaluation comparison give quotientSystemInverseImage as before.
